subject: NovaSpace: embeddings latency spike after catalog refresh — urgent mitigation requested
messages:
From: Allen Park <allen@novaspace.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: sre@novaspace.com
Date: 2027-08-25T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Embeddings p95/p99 doubled after catalog refresh — urgent

Hi Lauren,

We saw a sudden spike in embeddings latency for our production index starting ~23:58 UTC on 2027-08-24 (right after your model catalog refresh). Our p95 went from ~120ms to ~780ms and p99 is now >2.6s. This is affecting vector search and several downstream features — we have support tickets piling up.

Attached is a small graph showing the p95/p99 trend and the request IDs for a sample window (p95_p99_trends.png). Our SRE team observed an increase in request errors and timeouts on the hosted embeddings endpoint.

We need an immediate mitigation: either route NovaSpace traffic to the previous catalog variant or roll the catalog change back. Please advise ETA and any short-term workarounds. We’ll also need an SLA credit assessment. This is impacting paying customers in our search product.

Thanks,
Allen Park
Head of Platform Engineering, NovaSpace
allen@novaspace.com

Subject: Re: Embeddings p95/p99 doubled after catalog refresh — triage notes

Looping in SRE and infra notes from an initial look.

Summary of findings so far (quick):
- Catalog refresh at 2027-08-24 23:56:12 UTC deployed a new variant (v3.2-quant) for many customers.
- The new variant changed the recommended execution kernel and introduced a different int8 quantization path for the embedder.
- For large batch sizes (>64) we’re seeing a suboptimal kernel path that increases tail latency; this is more pronounced on our older GPU instance types where NovaSpace is routed.
- No obvious memory leaks or OOMs; error rate increase correlates with timeouts at p99 due to long tail.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Pin NovaSpace traffic to previous variant (v3.1-ctl) — minimal risk, fast.
2) Force lower batch size for NovaSpace routes (reduce concurrency) — reduces throughput but can lower p99.
3) Emergency rollback of catalog — higher blast radius, slower.

Attachments: catalog-change-log.txt (short changelist showing v3.2-quant rollout windows and kernel metadata).

Markus/Hannah — can you confirm whether a pin can be done per-customer without a full rollback? If yes we should do that now.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

We can do a per-customer pin; infra supports routing overrides. Required steps:
- Create a routing rule for NovaSpace to v3.1-ctl (takes ~12–20 minutes to propagate).
- Monitor p95/p99 for 30–60 min; if metrics normalize, keep pin until a safe fix is deployed.
- If pinning doesn’t fully restore tail behavior, schedule emergency rollback window (ETA 3 hours from approval) — rollback requires a config push and coordinated validation.

I recommend we pin now and hold rollback as a fallback. I’ll start the routing rule once I get approval from Lauren.

Also: Finance/Legal note — we’ll need guidance on SLA credits; please indicate whether NovaSpace escalation requires an immediate credit hold while we investigate.

Subject: Re: Embeddings p95/p99 doubled after catalog refresh — remediation complete

Allen — final update and next steps.

What we did:
- 2027-08-25 09:40 UTC: We pinned NovaSpace traffic to v3.1-ctl within the routing layer. Propagation completed ~09:55 UTC.
- 2027-08-25 10:20 UTC: Observed p95/p99 return to baseline for your traffic sample (graphs attached).
- We validated behavior across your primary regions and instance types; no functional regressions found.

Root cause (short):
- The catalog refresh introduced v3.2-quant which selected a quantization kernel that is performant on our newest GPU fleet but exhibits a long tail on older instances. The routing decision did not account for per-customer instance affinity, so customers routed to older pool experienced higher tail latency.

Remediation and forward actions:
1) Short-term: Keep NovaSpace pinned to v3.1-ctl until we complete a targeted backport of kernel heuristics (ETA 10 business days).
2) Mid-term: We’re adding per-customer routing affinities and a preflight canary test for catalog refreshes to catch kernel-affinity mismatches.
3) Credits: We will apply a one-time credit equivalent to 10% of August hosted embeddings invoice for NovaSpace while we finalize the postmortem and fix. Details will be shared by our billing team with a formal statement.

Attachments: p95_p99_trends.png (updated baseline vs. pinned)

I’m very sorry for the disruption. I’ll set up a 30-minute exec sync tomorrow if you’d like to go over the postmortem and the timeline for the permanent fix. Please let me know a convenient time for your CTO.

Thanks for your patience — we’ll treat this with high priority and follow through until you’re comfortable.
